proposals.expected_failure_mode: If admissions are driven by a distinct hospitalization process (not just lagged infections), delayed_I may misrepresent peak timing/width and underfit post-peak tails.
proposals.rationale: Hospitalization-rate target plausibly reflects infections with a reporting/admission lag; SEIRS supports moderate peakiness with potential within-season susceptibility replenishment while remaining parsimonious for a 31-week training window.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: May under-capture prolonged or multi-hump dynamics if immunity waning/re-susceptibility is material within the observed period.
proposals.rationale: Simpler than SEIRS and often sufficient for a single-season wave; delayed_I aligns with admission lag while reducing identifiability burden relative to adding an H compartment.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: H dynamics can be weakly identifiable in short series; may over-parameterize and yield unstable forecasts or confound H with I progression.
proposals.rationale: Directly maps the hospitalization-rate target to an explicit H compartment, matching surveillance semantics without requiring an ad hoc delay parameter.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If the target is closer to incident admissions only, I+H can bias level/shape and blur peak timing by attributing signal to the wrong compartment.
proposals.rationale: Allows observed hospitalizations to reflect a mixture of infectious burden and hospitalized prevalence, accommodating surveillance that may blend admission timing with ongoing inpatient occupancy effects.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Fractional order may absorb noise/seasonal forcing artifacts, reducing interpretability and potentially over-smoothing sharp changes in hospitalization rates.
proposals.rationale: Fractional dynamics can flexibly represent heterogeneous contact/progression and moderate peakiness; a 1-week delay captures short admission lag while keeping the observation model simple.
